request_flow.summary: Controller admits dev/test routes with verification fixtures. Trusted ordinary-entry configuration takes precedence and requires eligible C-02; it never falls back to P8-12. Historical fixture entry independently selects the prior historical templates and two-argument copy reader, without C-02. Request GET/POST checks the selected email scope; Identity receives the context explicitly. The new forgot-password login navigation renders only when ordinary development entry and C-02 are both eligible; historical-only login never consumes that WELL-136 link copy.
Identity canonicalizes email and locale, accepts only an existing eligible Account, then locks Account and performs idempotent request handling within an Ash transaction.

Under the Account lock, a new request supersedes current proofs and creates a 15-minute proof with fixed claims, Account binding, locale and request UUID. The selected server context fixes the email render schema. Communications checks current eligibility for that schema and establishes the content-bound intent in the same Identity transaction. Ineligible Content rolls back supersession, proof creation and intent together.

Executor checks the source, current Content and render eligibility, then commits attempt admission before it invokes the configured deterministic test provider outside authoritative transactions. Communications owns the unknown provider submission and reconciliation state; this never proves Identity reset completion.

GET/HEAD only render the explicit form. CSRF-protected POST invokes Identity reset. Identity locks Account/proof, verifies current claims, rejects current password, consumes proof and writes credential/security consequences atomically.

security_invariants.summary: Request response is neutral and bounded; invalid, unknown, ineligible, timeout and internal failure do not disclose Account existence.

Ordinary WELL-136 requires dev/test verification fixtures and exact eligible EN/AF C-02. Historical P8-12 uses its existing separate copy and historical email approval. Neither path borrows the other copy scope or accepts request-selected context; unsupported locales fail closed. The C-02 login link also requires ordinary development entry; historical fixture admission alone grants no C-02 consumption.
Proof is purpose-bound, short-lived, single-use, bound to current Account security state and signing key; no direct token creation occurs during delivery.
No automatic login or Session issuance follows reset; existing sessions and trusted devices are revoked.
No production provider or participant release authority is added; delivery uses the deterministic test provider.

Historical unavailable and uncertain outcomes return an empty 503 because no historical wording covers them; they never borrow C-02 or present uncertainty as confirmed failure. Ordinary WELL-136 retains its exact service and uncertainty messages.

concurrency.summary: Account row lock serializes issuance, supersession and consumption; proof row lock protects explicit consumption; transaction spans Account, Token, Session, DeviceAssurance, RegistrationOperation and EvidenceObligation.

idempotency_retry.summary: Same request operation UUID finds the prior Token and performs no second issuance or context retargeting. A new eligible request operation supersedes extant proof only if its selected Content scope remains eligible.
Same confirmation UUID on consumed proof returns prior :already_reset without reapplying password. A different operation against consumed proof fails closed.
Request timeout cancels bounded worker; transaction rollback protects interrupted writes. If commit wins cancellation, same operation retry is harmless.
Reset transaction errors that cannot confirm commit return :reset_uncertain; do not report confirmed failure or retry side effects automatically.

failure_recovery.summary: Missing, withdrawn or corrupt Phase-9 applicability does not disable historical P8-12 issuance or delivery when its own approval remains valid. An explicit WELL-136 request still fails closed, rolling back attempted historical proof supersession. Historical delivery separately fails closed on withdrawal of its own approval.
Any failed write in reset transaction rolls back proof consumption, credential replacement, revocations and security evidence together.
Exceptions/uncertain transaction results map to reset_uncertain; invalid proof and validation failure map to reset_unavailable.
Delivery invocation uncertainty belongs to Communications provider reconciliation; delivery evidence never proves reset completion.

Migration down restores the legacy-only message_intents schema check. It will fail while any row has render_schema password-reset-well136-v1. The owner must reconcile this rollback hazard under an authorized procedure; the map prescribes no deletion or transformation.

TEST browser entry uses P805 guardian restoration of the exact prior fp001_development_entry value or absence, even after monitored owner death. Setup atomically creates an owned temporary directory before fallible copying; nested cleanup stops its started server and removes its directory on setup/body failure. This never authorizes retained database cleanup.

If C-02 disappears or changes between admission and result rendering, the ordinary controller catches only the typed Content availability exception and returns empty HTTP 503 with no-store and no-referrer. No stale text, fallback, outcome declaration or automatic business retry is sent. Rollback, committed and committed-but-uncertain outcomes retain their owner state; an unchanged operation can recover after Content eligibility returns. Buffered rendering sends no partial body.
